title: Recording: You’re Sixteen, Oh My My by Ringo Starr | 1973
content:
Sunset Sound Recorders, Los Angeles
Producer: Richard Perry
Engineer: Bill Schnee

The second recording session for Ringo Starr’s third studio album, Ringo, took place on 6 March 1973.

Two tracks were worked on: ‘You’re Sixteen’ and ‘Oh My My’.

The backing track for ‘You’re Sixteen’ had been recorded the previous day. The overdubs added on this day included Harry Nilsson’s doo-wop backing vocals.

‘Oh My My’ was the second song worked on, with overdubs following on 7 and 14 March and 12 May. The song features two drum tracks, by Starr and Jim Keltner, and backing vocals by Merry Clayton and Martha Reeves.

Without any lawyers knowing anything about it, we came back to LA, and in five days had recorded five tracks, which included the three major singles from the album, ‘Photograph’, ‘You’re Sixteen’ and ‘Oh My My’.
Richard Perry
The Record Producers, John Tobler and Stuart Grundy
